title: Motion Has Geometry Too
hook: Tracking and optical flow treat every pixel as drifting on its own. But real objects are rigid — points on the same body move together, so give motion a basis instead of a per-pixel guess.
key_points: Geometry foundation models pushed monocular 3D reconstruction forward; extending them to 4D dynamic scenes is the open problem.
Sparse tracking and dense point-wise flow model motion as independent per-point displacements, ignoring that real objects obey rigid-body kinematics.
The premise: physical motion is structured — objects undergo rigid-body transformations governed by SE(3), not unstructured displacements.
Structure-of-Motion decomposes scene dynamics into a compact set of motion bases, each a temporal sequence of 6D twists in SE(3).
Dense motion is recovered by sparse, time-shared per-pixel assignment weights over those bases, so points on one object share a rigid-body trajectory.
A parallel motion-geometry encoder and decoder infer 3D geometry, world-coordinate motion, and kinematic structure in one forward pass from monocular RGB video.
content_html: Geometry foundation models have substantially advanced monocular 3D reconstruction, but extending that to 4D — dynamic scenes over time — is still open. Lin and colleagues argue the obstacle is representational. Most motion-perception methods, whether sparse tracking or dense point-wise flow, treat motion as independent per-point displacements. Real-world objects don't move that way: they obey rigid-body kinematics, so their points move collectively. Motion itself has geometric structure, in the form of rigid-body transformations governed by SE(3).
extra_html:
Structure-of-Motion

SM4RT is a transformer for end-to-end 3D reconstruction and structured motion perception, built on a representation the authors call Structure-of-Motion. Scene motion is decomposed into a compact set of motion bases, each represented as a temporal sequence of 6D twists in SE(3). Dense scene motion is then recovered through sparse, time-shared per-pixel assignment weights over those bases — which is the mechanism that forces points on the same object to share a common rigid-body motion trajectory instead of each drifting independently.

The architecture

A parallel motion-geometry encoder and decoder jointly infer three things in a single forward pass from monocular RGB video: 3D geometry, motion in world coordinates, and the scene's kinematic structure. The authors report strong motion-reconstruction performance while preserving the geometric structure of scene motion — the recurring lesson being that building a physical prior into the representation tends to beat regressing an unconstrained field and hoping coherence emerges.

related.title: Video Generation Models Are General-Purpose Vision Learners
related.hook: Next-token prediction turned NLP into a generalist. This paper argues text-to-video generation can do the same for vision — one backbone, many tasks, beating specialists.

flashcards.prompt: What assumption do sparse tracking and dense optical flow make that this paper rejects?
flashcards.back_html: That motion is a set of independent point-wise displacements. Real objects obey rigid-body kinematics, so points on the same body move collectively rather than in isolation.

flashcards.prompt: How does Structure-of-Motion represent a scene's dynamics?

choices.text: As a compact set of motion bases, each a temporal sequence of 6D twists in SE(3)
As a dense per-pixel displacement field regressed independently at each frame
As a single global camera transform plus a residual depth map per frame

flashcards.explanation_html: The bases carry the rigid-body structure; dense motion then comes from sparse, time-shared per-pixel assignment weights over them, which is what forces points on one object onto a common trajectory.

flashcards.prompt: What does the assignment-weight design buy you?
flashcards.back_html: Because weights are sparse and shared across time, points assigned to the same basis necessarily follow a common rigid-body motion trajectory — the object's coherence is built into the representation rather than hoped for.
